hero.title: From “this is not working” to a clear next step.
hero.lede: You bring the problem. LDW starts by understanding what is happening now, what you want to work better, and what already needs to stay intact before recommending technology.

steps.title: Assess
steps.description: Start with the friction, desired outcome, current systems, ownership, constraints, cost, privacy, security, and support needs. The goal is to understand the real problem before choosing a tool.

steps.title: Improve or build
steps.description: Keep what is already useful. Configure, integrate, automate, modernize, or repair first when that solves the problem well; build a focused missing piece only when a real gap remains.

steps.title: Handoff or care
steps.description: Leave ownership, deployment, access, recovery, rollback, and maintenance understandable. Ongoing care can continue when it creates value, but basic ownership should not depend on keeping LDW forever.

beforeBuild.title: Four questions usually matter more than the framework.

items.title: What are you trying to make easier?
items.description: Define the business outcome first so the implementation does not become the goal.

items.title: What already works?
items.description: Preserve useful systems, data, and staff habits where practical instead of replacing everything by default.

items.title: Who owns the important pieces?
items.description: Domains, repositories, hosting, data, and administrative access should have a clear owner and recovery path.

items.title: What will this cost to keep?
items.description: Consider recurring services, maintenance effort, portability, support burden, and future change before adding infrastructure.

principles.title: The work should stay understandable.
items: Secure named access and least practical privilege
Open standards and portable source where practical
Low recurring cost when it meets the need
Clear testing, documentation, validation, and rollback

handoff.title: You should not need LDW forever just to understand what you own.
handoff.body: A good final state makes ownership, deployment, access, maintenance, recovery, and the next decision understandable. When continued support makes sense, it can be provided without turning basic ownership into a subscription requirement.

expect.eyebrow: What working together should feel like
expect.title: Direct conversation, explainable choices, and no pressure to make the solution bigger than it needs to be.

items.title: Talk with the person doing the work
items.description: The same owner-operated model that starts the conversation carries through delivery and handoff.

items.title: Understand the tradeoffs
items.description: Important choices should be explained in plain language, including cost, support, ownership, portability, privacy, and security.

items.title: Change consequential systems deliberately
items.description: Production, ownership, access, and other consequential changes should have a known current state, proposed state, validation path, and rollback.

items.title: Be willing not to build
items.description: A useful outcome can be a configuration change, an existing maintained service, a small repair, or a recommendation to leave a working system alone.
